entries.title: Choose an instance and credential
entries.pageTitle: Read and create your first event
entries.text: Use the HTTP-actions origin of your intended instance plus /api/v2. Obtain an API key from Settings → Account → API Keys in that instance. Keep the key in your terminal or secret manager. Never put an owner secret in a browser bundle. Source-verified examples require an instance running the matching API; hosted deployment and registry release are not established here.

entries.title: Read your events
entries.pageTitle: Read and create your first event
entries.text: First verify the account with GET /profile, then list accessible events. REST v2 returns resource bodies directly, rather than the v1 success/data wrapper.

entries.title: Empty success and pagination
entries.pageTitle: Read and create your first event
entries.text: An empty list is a successful response. With pagination=cursor the envelope is {items: [], nextCursor: null}. Continue using the opaque nextCursor until it is null, including after an empty page. Do not parse or manufacture cursors. Without pagination, some operations retain legacy arrays; consult each operation.

entries.title: Create one event
entries.pageTitle: Read and create your first event
entries.text: Generate and retain the request identifier before sending the request. The JSON response contains eventId. Fixed times need an explicit UTC offset; this minimal example creates an undated event.

entries.title: Recover an uncertain create
entries.pageTitle: Read and create your first event
entries.text: For this event creation example, retry an uncertain response with the same Idempotency-Key, same identity and identical body within 24 hours of its Unix-millisecond timestamp. A conflict or expired identifier requires inspection, not a new blind create. Other writes have operation-specific guarantees: inspect current state before deliberately resubmitting. Do not automatically retry arbitrary mutations.

entries.title: Account authority and credential bounds
entries.pageTitle: Read and create your first event
entries.text: A credential never grants more than the account’s current authority. Organizer and moderator roles belong to an event; a platform administrator is a separate role. A collection scope is not an event-specific grant. Verify distinct organizer and attendee identities independently with /profile; an attendee attempting organizer-only management must receive permission denied. 401 means credential/account eligibility; 403 means insufficient scope or current authority. Do not switch to an owner key to conceal the denial.

entries.title: Start with general programming prerequisites
entries.pageTitle: Run, test and submit a contribution
entries.text: Use Git, Node.js 22 or 24 and pnpm 10.12.1 (the root packageManager). React/TypeScript familiarity helps for UI work; Convex knowledge is introduced progressively. Clone the current repository and install its locked dependencies. A focused shared-package test does not require a live account or credentials.

entries.title: Run one focused check
entries.pageTitle: Run, test and submit a contribution
entries.text: The shared GDL conformance suite is a useful first success with no service credentials. Run the workspace quality checks before submission. If pnpm reports an unsupported runtime, use Node 22 or 24; if the lock is stale, confirm the branch instead of rewriting it blindly. Humans can follow the repository development setup for servers; automated agents must use already-running services and must never run dev, start, build or Convex deployment commands.

entries.title: Submit a reviewed contribution
entries.pageTitle: Run, test and submit a contribution
entries.text: Create a focused branch, explain the affected user flow and tests in your pull request, and follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Include a changeset for a user-facing change after agreeing its summary with the maintainer. Review permissions, compatibility and accessibility before requesting review. Never commit environment files or credentials.

entries.title: Develop a source handler and component
entries.text: Source contributors use defineAddonHandler, register the branded handler in the backend registry and register an explicit frontend AddonDefinition. Standard AddonContext scopes data to the current event and add-on. Lifecycle hooks cover enable/configuration, participant data and event changes; trusted rawCtx is privileged source code, not a sandbox for arbitrary downloaded code. Follow the existing bring-list handler as a bounded starting point, validate all configuration and add a component to the explicit catalog.
entries.identifiers: Develop a source handler and component

entries.title: Verify the scoped handler through a real fixture workflow
entries.text: The source above is the current bring-list handler in convex/addons/handlers/bringList.ts. Its existing registry entry is in convex/addons/registry.ts and its frontend definition is in packages/web/features/addons/runtime/catalog.ts. Run the authenticated REST/CLI participation fixture to observe scoped configuration, participant validation and disabled-state cleanup without a live account. This fixture does not establish hosted notification or integration delivery.
entries.identifiers: Verify the scoped handler through a real fixture workflow

entries.title: Author a reusable add-on template
entries.text: An add-on template is a reusable definition; an event add-on uses its saved snapshot. Editing or deleting a template does not rewrite existing event configurations. For the CLI author path, first confirm addonAuthoring.version: 1 from the intended instance. Save this bounded portable definition as meal.json, then import it as a new private draft. Source/local availability is established; registry installation is not claimed.

entries.title: Import, inspect and deliberately publish
entries.text: Capture TEMPLATE_ID and saved version from the import response. Inspect the saved definition before publishing and enabling it on an event you may manage. Concurrent versions fail without applying the write. If a response is uncertain, get the definition before trying again. These commands use the current generated CLI reference.

entries.title: Check authorization and event isolation
entries.text: Template ownership is independent of event organizer/moderator authority. Participant submissions use the authenticated identity, with no impersonation. Verify one event cannot read another event’s add-on data, and denied writes cause no side effects. A template is declarative data, not a dynamically installable arbitrary-code marketplace. send_webhook is unsupported for new authoring; configured actions can have side effects and must be inspected. See the existing authenticated REST participation and authoring fixtures for verification.

entries.title: Use the verified source artifact
entries.text: CLI 0.1.0 is available in this repository. Use Node 22 or 24 and the locked workspace installation. No registry publication is established by these docs; do not assume an npm beta is available. The local executable supplies the exact command catalog.

entries.title: Choose an instance, profile and identity
entries.text: Choose both the REST v2 URL and authorization website from the same intended instance. After explicit browser login, verify the account before every sensitive workflow. Temporary environment keys must match GROUPI_API_KEY_PROFILE; --api-key-stdin reads a temporary key without saving it. Stored credentials use the OS keychain when available. Browser CLI authorization is distinct from delegated third-party sign-in.
entries.identifiers: Choose an instance, profile and identity

entries.title: Read and create using structured output
entries.text: Use --format json and a trusted installed executable (or node packages/cli/bin/groupi.js from source). Exit codes: 0 success; 1 unexpected failure; 2 usage/validation/conflict/cancelled confirmation; 3 authentication/permission; 4 resource or endpoint missing; 5 network/rate-limit/unsupported-server/uncertain outcome. Inspect errors and the process exit status; JSON output does not make a failed process successful. Verify distinct organizer/attendee profiles using auth status. Retain a generated request identifier before creating; use the same identifier and unchanged arguments for an uncertain protected create.
entries.identifiers: Read and create using structured output

entries.title: Continue pages and recover failures
entries.text: List commands support --limit and --cursor; --all explicitly retrieves all pages. Continue until nextCursor is null, including empty pages. A malformed continuation fails; preserve the reported error rather than treating incomplete data as a complete list. Writes are not automatically retried. After an uncertain unprotected write, inspect current server state before resubmission. auth logout --revoke revokes the selected stored credential; temporary keys are independent.

entries.title: Domain-owned backend operations
entries.text: Reusable operations live with their domain. Native Convex functions and versioned REST routes adapt verified identity to those operations; version folders own HTTP contracts, not business behavior. Each write transaction checks the actor’s current permissions. HTTP preflight alone cannot protect against authority changing between calls.

entries.title: Shared logic and platform UI
entries.text: Cross-platform logic belongs in packages/shared, which never imports Next.js, Expo or React Native. Platform adapters supply navigation, storage and toast behavior. Web is client-only; live application data uses Convex useQuery/useMutation. Feature modules own their UI and hooks, and reusable presentation follows atoms, molecules, organisms and data-free templates.

entries.title: Organizer, moderator and platform administrator
entries.text: An organizer or moderator has a role in an individual event. A platform administrator has authority over an installation and is a separate concept. Event membership and RSVP are separate: joining does not confirm attendance. Current authority is checked for the operation being performed.

entries.title: Groups, invite lists and audiences
entries.text: A Group is a formal membership community. An invite list is a private saved selection of existing users; editing it sends no invitation and changes no membership. An event audience determines visibility eligibility, independently of event membership, invitations and RSVP. A friend relationship is independent of shared Group membership.

entries.title: REST v2
entries.text: REST v2 is recommended for new integrations and is the CLI transport. Resource responses are direct JSON; page and delete envelopes are operation-specific. Source-generated references describe this checkout. They are not proof that a hosted instance has this release. Verify the target instance before executing examples.

entries.title: REST v1
entries.text: REST v1 remains separately documented. Most resource successes wrap success/data. Do not assume path similarity means wire or authorization equivalence with v2. No retirement date or maintenance duration is currently promised. Select v1 explicitly for its generated reference.

entries.title: Proposed Linux Compose journey
entries.text: A supported Linux Compose installation, enrollment, backup/restore and recovery journey is proposed and excluded from this implementation. Existing profile URL selection does not certify self-hosting. There is no runnable installation quickstart here. Self-hosting is not a launch dependency of this portal.

entries.title: Source candidates and published packages
entries.text: The repository contains unpublished TypeScript and Python REST v2 SDK candidates. TypeScript supports Node.js 22 and 24; Python requires 3.11 or later and provides synchronous and asynchronous clients. Publication, hosted API compatibility and additional runtime support require separate release evidence. Use the source package instructions rather than assuming a registry package is available.

entries.title: Specific request and response types
entries.text: Named SDK methods derive their inputs and results from the current OpenAPI operation catalog. TypeScript declarations and Python TypedDict models describe known fields, required arguments, literal choices and nullable results. Python includes runtime-importable schema types and py.typed metadata. Source freshness and positive and negative consumer type checks guard the generated contracts. Static types do not validate every response field from an arbitrary server at runtime.

entries.title: Read Events with an explicit instance and credential
entries.text: Use a server-side owner credential for this legacy API-key example. Keep it out of browser bundles. Iteration follows opaque cursors, including empty pages, and raises an error on malformed or repeated continuations. Use the explicit bounded-key or delegated credential mode when the intended workflow has narrower grants.
entries.identifiers: Read Events with an explicit instance and credential

entries.title: Use Python sync or async adapters
entries.text: Groupi is synchronous; AsyncGroupi runs standard-library I/O in a worker thread. Cancelling an await cannot undo a write already sent by that worker. Connected sockets have bounded deadlines, while operating-system DNS resolution can exceed the deadline before a socket exists. The Python package README documents this runtime limit and uncertain-write errors.
entries.identifiers: Use Python sync or async adapters

entries.title: Handle uncertainty without duplicate writes
entries.text: Reads have bounded retries; writes never retry automatically. Errors preserve status and uncertainty. Persist an Event creation replay key and the unchanged body before sending, then deliberately reuse that key after an uncertain response within the server retention window. Inspect state before repeating other writes. Capability checks verify the selected instance; they never substitute a different host or a broader credential.

entries.title: Keep delegated tokens bound to the approved client
entries.text: DelegatedSession supports the approved native and confidential-web authorization-code profile with S256, state and an explicit issuer, audience, instance and client. Confidential web callers supply their own private-key assertion signer. Background refresh is separately consented and cannot expand access. Restored token state retains these bindings. The API adapter does not treat an unverified identity token as a signed-in user and never opens a browser or falls back to an owner key during an API call. See the SDK source README for the exact exchange and persistence interfaces.
entries.identifiers: Keep delegated tokens bound to the approved client

entries.title: Connect a member to Group Discord
entries.text: Request groups.discord.read and groups.discord.connect with fresh selected-Group consent. readOwnGroupDiscordStatus returns own progress and an Open Discord destination. beginOwnGroupDiscordConnect takes an exact registered HTTPS returnUrl and returns a short-lived Groupi-hosted link for member identity and explicit consent. Python exposes read_own_group_discord_status and begin_own_group_discord_connect. Re-read status on return; pending, screening, cleanup failures and external exceptions are distinct from completed access. These member scopes expose no Discord credentials or manager configuration authority.
entries.identifiers: Connect a member to Group Discord

entries.title: Realtime and planned SDK improvements
entries.text: The selected design adds optional Convex subscription modules while preserving the dependency-free REST core, with durable change delivery designed separately. Runtime response validation, browser realtime support, subscription credentials and the durable feed are future implementation targets. The evolution guide outlines resources, authentication, expiry, reconnects, limits, compatibility, replay, retention and release evidence; it does not announce available packages or endpoints.

entries.title: Current availability
entries.text: The unpublished REST v2 SDK candidates cover 238 operations with specific TypeScript declarations and Python TypedDict models, bounded retries, pagination and delegated sessions. Realtime modules, subscription credential exchange, durable change feeds, general integration webhooks and complete runtime response validation are not implemented. Static types and runtime-importable Python models do not validate arbitrary server responses. Planned browser support does not change today's Node-only TypeScript SDK support or delegated-client profiles.

entries.title: Selected architecture
entries.text: Keep the REST core dependency-free and provide optional SDK modules backed by Convex subscriptions. Groupi owns versioned public views and types; consumers do not import private application function paths. Durable delivery has a separate contract. ADR-0007 records this direction. CLI/TUI transport continues under ADR-0001; adopting subscriptions there requires its own decision. The maintainer selected this direction and recommended design defaults on 15 October 2026; the following sections describe those planned contracts.

entries.title: Convex realtime subscriptions
entries.text: A reactive client subscribes to a query over a WebSocket. Convex tracks its database dependencies and updates the result when relevant writes commit, keeping a client's subscriptions consistent with a database snapshot. Changes through REST, web or mobile can update the same view. Ordinary REST requests remain point-in-time reads. Public queries need focused indexes, bounded joins and small projections to control invalidation work and payload size.

entries.title: Live views and durable change records
entries.text: A live resource view presents the latest permitted state, such as an attendee list. Intermediate states may be coalesced; reconnect retrieves current state. A change record describes an occurrence such as an RSVP change. Durable consumers need ordering, retention and replay after downtime. Live revisions, durable feed cursors and REST pagination cursors are distinct. A Groupi Event is the gathering; a change record is an occurrence about a resource.
entries.identifiers: Live views and durable change records

entries.title: Initial resource views and permissions
entries.text: Initially target authorized Event summary/detail, attendee/RSVP views, posts and replies. Require events.read, members.read or discussion.read respectively; attachments additionally require files.read. Attendee fields follow the current Event visibility policy: public projection means permitted to this caller, not anonymous access. Private RSVP notes, attendee email and unrelated profile fields remain excluded. RSVP viewing does not grant RSVP mutation. Group, invitation and add-on streams follow separately defined actions and grants.

entries.title: Optional modules and runtimes
entries.text: Target Node.js 22/24, Python 3.11 or later and browser TypeScript ES modules. Working package names are @groupi/sdk-realtime and groupi-sdk[realtime]; neither is available to install yet. Convex/WebSocket dependencies belong only to optional modules and must not load with REST-core imports. Python consumption is async. Framework hooks are separate adapters. React Native/Expo and other native clients follow after lifecycle, backgrounding, callback and secure-storage verification. Actual supported versions require release-matrix evidence.

entries.title: Typed subscription interface
entries.text: Provide named typed resource watches, snapshots, discriminated connection states, an error channel and explicit unsubscribe. Python also provides async iteration and context-managed cleanup. Snapshots include contract version, opaque view revision and freshness metadata. Revision equality supports deduplication within a view; it is not a global transaction timestamp or replay cursor. This example illustrates the intended interface only and is not executable today.

entries.title: Live windows and pagination
entries.text: Initial design limits are 20 items by default, 100 maximum per live list window, 4 MiB per decoded message and 20 distinct watches per client context. Servers advertise and enforce their limits; these defaults are not measured capacity guarantees. Share identical watches only within the same instance, credential, contract and query context. Historical pages use REST pagination. Merging them with a changing live window requires ID-based deduplication and refresh and does not promise an immutable snapshot or gap-free history across pages.

entries.title: Connection status and stale data
entries.text: Expose connecting, live, reconnecting, closed and error states. Retain the last snapshot during transient transport loss, explicitly marked stale with its last observation time. Authorization denial stops the affected watch and invalidates inaccessible SDK-held data. Reduced field grants remove those fields from an otherwise permitted view. Identity or instance switches clear their subscription context. Applications may already hold copies that the SDK cannot erase.

entries.title: Reconnection and cancellation
entries.text: Use exponential backoff with jitter, capped at 30 seconds between reconnect attempts. Reauthorize and fetch a fresh snapshot before reporting live. Auth, contract and permission failures are explicit errors, not reasons to change host, widen credentials or open consent UI. Unsubscribe, AbortSignal and Python context exit/cancellation stop future callbacks and release owned watches. Reconnection does not replay missed changes.

entries.title: Subscription credentials
entries.text: Exchange a supported bounded key or delegated REST access token through an authenticated endpoint for a separate read-only realtime JWT. Reject legacy collection/owner keys for exchange. Maximum lifetime is five minutes, capped by source credential and grant expiry. Pin issuer, instance, deployment, dedicated audience and contract version; reference an opaque principal/session. Permission is the intersection of issued bounds and live authority. Raw source secrets never enter query arguments, URLs or logs. JWTs cannot renew themselves or grant writes; ordinary native app functions must reject realtime identities.

entries.title: Browser authentication
entries.text: Use a confidential web application's backend to retain refresh credentials and signing keys and exchange current authorization for ephemeral realtime JWTs. The browser obtains them through its own authenticated backend and holds them in memory. It receives no owner key, bounded service key, confidential key or refresh token. This permits browser consumption without browser-only OAuth refresh; that public-client profile remains a separately reviewed extension. Server SDKs exchange credentials from their secure server context. Ordinary watches never trigger interactive sign-in.

entries.title: Current authority and revocation
entries.text: Each allowlisted query reads its exchange/session record and relevant credential, grant, app, account, membership and policy records so changes invalidate the view. Derive resource parents server-side. A signature does not freeze permission until expiry, and capabilities never confer authority. Use a separate Convex client per instance/credential context. Revocation denies subsequent authorized evaluations in committed transaction order; buffered, delivered or copied data cannot be recalled. Unrelated authorized watches can remain live.

entries.title: Time-based expiry
entries.text: Wall-clock passage alone does not rerun a Convex query. A time check in a cached query, client heartbeat or client-supplied now value cannot be the security boundary. Server/transport checks must reject new protected results after expiry; JWT expiry cannot exceed source expiry. Scheduled server-record invalidation is defense in depth without exact timing promises. Clients renew through a valid source credential. At JWT expiry, invalidate its held result even if renewal is pending; resume only after authenticated confirmation. An idle disconnected client may retain earlier data; expiry is not remote erasure.

entries.title: Runtime response validation
entries.text: Generate dependency-free validators from the same versioned contracts as SDK types. Validate REST successes, subscription snapshots and supported error/page envelopes by default. Check required fields, known types, nullability, variants and enums; tolerate additive object fields and expose the declared typed resource projection. Incompatible responses raise typed INVALID_RESPONSE errors. Preserve uncertain-write classification if the server may have committed first. Reject incompatible snapshots before callbacks receive them, without silently changing contracts.

entries.title: Compatibility and discovery
entries.text: Negotiate versioned subscription contracts and advertised resources before connecting. Unsupported instances produce typed compatibility errors without silent polling or host fallback. Cache successful REST version/capability discovery in memory for 60 seconds by canonical instance/API major, share in-flight work, offer explicit refresh and invalidate incompatible responses. Never cache permission decisions or permanently cache failures. Additive fields are compatible; removals, changed types and unknown closed-enum values require explicit version or compatibility handling.

entries.title: Write replay and recovery
entries.text: Retain bounded read retries and no automatic write retries. Advertise replay support, retention and key requirements per operation; accepting Idempotency-Key does not make arbitrary writes replay-safe. Recover supported uncertain creates using the persisted identical key/body within retention, with current permissions governing recovery responses. Inspect other writes only where an authorized read can establish the outcome; otherwise retain uncertainty. Live observations are not acknowledgements that a particular write committed exactly once.

entries.title: Separate durable delivery
entries.text: Use a transactional outbox and authenticated REST cursor pull for durable recovery. Signed HTTPS webhooks adapt the same records. Initial families target Event changed, RSVP changed and post/reply created/changed/deleted. Record changes in the same domain-owned transaction as their effects, using stable change IDs, resource IDs, type/schema version and minimal metadata. Avoid copied private discussion/profile bodies by default. This independently gated phase is separate from initial live views.

entries.title: Change ordering and cursors
entries.text: Use immutable unique change IDs and monotonic sequence numbers within each parent Event stream. Consumers tolerate duplicates and deduplicate by change ID; there is no global or webhook arrival ordering guarantee. Pull retrieves eligible retained records in stream order. Bind opaque cursors to instance, grant, filters and schema version. Initial pull is scoped to one Event stream; multi-Event merge ordering and cursors are deferred. Publish continuation only after fully scanning a page. Empty pages may continue. Consumers persist progress after durable processing, not receipt. There is no exactly-once delivery promise.

entries.title: Retention and recovery gaps
entries.text: The initial retention target is seven days with explicit retention floor and high-water mark. Replay/delivery remains subject to retention and current authority. Expired cursors return HTTP 410 with CURSOR_EXPIRED and resynchronization guidance; never silently jump ahead. A fresh snapshot recovers present state, not lost business history. Consumers that require every occurrence must alert and reconcile gaps. Live revisions and reconnects do not extend durable retention.

entries.title: Historical access and deletion
entries.text: Check authority during selection, replay and dispatch. History requires eligibility at occurrence and current authority; new grants do not automatically expose old private changes. Retain enough eligibility evidence to prove access or deny records whose eligibility is unproven. Event deletion removes current Event authority; prior eligibility alone does not authorize subsequent external replay or dispatch. Event-deleted records may be retained internally, but external delivery is deferred until a separate deletion-only authorization contract is approved. Post/reply deletion may produce minimal tombstones while the parent Event exists and current authority remains valid. Revocation stops future dispatch/replay. Authorized refetch returns current state; inaccessible or deleted resources use a non-enumerating response and never imply access to historical bodies.

entries.title: Signed webhooks
entries.text: Use HTTPS and HMAC verification over raw body and timestamp, stable delivery/change IDs and rotating secrets. Retry with jitter for up to 24 hours, bounded by retention and current eligibility, and expose exhausted-delivery status. Successful 2xx acknowledges delivery; consumers persist before acknowledging and tolerate retries. Manual replay preserves original change IDs. Publish versioned envelopes and verification helpers. Existing notification webhooks and add-on actions are not this general delivery API.

entries.title: Webhook destination security
entries.text: Verify destination ownership, require HTTPS and refuse redirects. Validate all resolved IPv4/IPv6 addresses at registration and each connection; deny private, loopback, link-local and reserved destinations. Pin validated connection addresses while checking TLS hostname; enforce outbound network controls, timeouts and payload bounds. Changed destinations require verification again. Private self-hosted destinations need a separate operator policy outside this initial hosted design. Signing a delivery does not prevent SSRF.

entries.title: Authorization breadth and bulk work
entries.text: Expand external permissions around concrete Group, invitation and add-on workflows with explicit actions/resource selectors. SDK coverage does not confer those permissions, and reads never imply membership or management writes. Account and platform-admin operations remain separately controlled. General bulk writes are follow-up work: define per-item outcomes, partial success and recovery first, without implying an all-or-nothing transaction. Cursor iteration remains the default for large reads.

entries.title: Delivery phases and evidence
entries.text: First deliver contract-driven runtime validation and compatibility improvements, then optional live modules, versioned views and the credential bridge. Verify Node/Python/browser matrices, strict types, dependency isolation, limits, cancellation, reconnect, context switches, scope reduction and expiry before publication. Prove idle-expiry behavior followed by data mutations and suspended browser timers. Independently test durable transaction/replay/gap/duplicate and webhook SSRF behavior. Group/add-on streams and React Native follow their acceptance gates. Names, examples and design limits here do not certify release availability. Self-hosting and encryption remain deferred.

entries.title: Source references
entries.text: Groupi's bounded authorization, delegated sign-in and SDK contracts and ADR-0001/0003/0006/0007 define existing boundaries. Convex docs establish mechanisms, not the existence of the proposed Groupi bridge. Pin deployed versions and verify behavior before claiming release support. , , , , , , .

entries.title: Verify the authorization capability first
entries.text: Bounded credentials and delegated sign-in are source candidates in this repository. Verify the intended deployment before using them; this page does not establish a hosted release or configured OAuth issuer. Existing CLI browser login remains a separate flow. Credential bounds always intersect current account authority, and an authentication failure never switches to a broader key.

entries.title: Create a bounded key for selected Events
entries.text: In Account settings, use bounded keys to choose a name, expiry, explicit actions and selected Events. User keys may instead explicitly select all current and future Events within current authority. Identity-only user keys need no Event selection. Copy the secret when it is shown once and keep it out of browser bundles and source control. Legacy collection keys remain separately labeled and have different permissions.
entries.identifiers: Create a bounded key for selected Events

entries.title: Request each action and related field explicitly
entries.text: Event reads, updates, member reads, discussion actions, file access and identity claims have separate actions. Write-only access returns identifiers, not discussion content or attachment URLs. File uploads require a granted eventId and files.upload; attachment expansion requires files.read. Event creation, membership administration, Groups and Invite Lists are not supported bounded actions. An unsupported operation fails closed; use the published action matrix before designing a workflow.
entries.identifiers: Request each action and related field explicitly

entries.title: Give an integration its own discussion identity
entries.text: An integration key selects Events and requires a current Organizer sponsor. The integration appears as the author of its own posts and replies and has no person record, membership or RSVP. It can edit or delete only its own discussion content. Sponsor authority is rechecked for each operation; sponsorship does not grant blanket access or impersonate the sponsor.
entries.identifiers: Give an integration its own discussion identity

entries.title: Consent, background access and disconnect
entries.text: The approved delegated profile uses authorization code with S256 PKCE, app-and-instance-specific identity, 60-second codes and 5-minute access tokens. Background access requires separate consent; rotating refresh is limited to 30 days and 7 days of inactivity. Initial clients are confidential web and native apps; browser-only refresh is unavailable. Connected Apps shows actions and resources and lets you disconnect. Disconnect stops future access but cannot delete copied data or terminate the app’s own session. Release readiness still requires issuer configuration and environment-specific verification.

entries.title: Inspect and revoke access
entries.text: Revoked or expired credentials fail without a grace period. Current membership and role loss reduce effective access even if a key has not expired. Owner-visible audit metadata is retained for 90 days and excludes raw credentials and resource bodies. Already committed writes and previously acquired file URLs are not undone by revocation.

entries.text: Download Markdown or plain text for any page, or retrieve the public JSON passage index and llms.txt. Exports use the same canonical corpus, versions, availability and source hashes as the portal. No account, hosted answer assistant or authenticated machine-query service is needed. Private events, credentials and repository planning are excluded.
